game.coreLoop: SC2Mafia (custom SC2 Arcade map by Dark.Revenant, ~15 players, direct ancestor of Town of Salem) alternates three cycles: DAY, LYNCH (trial), and NIGHT. SETUP: host configures the game in a pre-game setup phase (players can vote -repick to replace host, -default to force the 'Setup of the Day'); then a naming phase where players pick names (-Name) or get random ones; roles are then secretly assigned. DAY CYCLE (1-6 min, host-set): all living players talk in public chat, share findings, whisper (-pm), and after an optional no-vote 'Discussion' period (30s-3min) vote to lynch via vote buttons next to player names. Day Type options: 'Majority' (51% of votes = instant execution), 'Majority + Trial' (51% puts player on trial — the de facto standard), 'Ballot' (secret ballot, most votes executed at day end), 'Ballot + Trial'. LYNCH CYCLE: accused player gets uninterrupted defense time (Trial Defense option; trial time 30s-2min split 50/50 defense/voting; 'Trial Pauses Day' option stops the day timer so an innocent verdict lets town vote again), then everyone votes guilty/innocent; guilty = public execution (flavor variants: firing squad, electrocution, sniper, gas chamber, hanging). Lynched player's role and Last Will are revealed immediately. -skip command (50%+ of living players) skips the day. NIGHT CYCLE (30s-2min): all players submit night actions simultaneously via UI/commands; Mafia/Triad/Cult/Masons/Jailor get private night chats; Mafia votes its kill target (-target). At dawn the game reveals deaths with role + Last Will (unless janitored), plus optional Death Descriptions (weapon flavor text identifying killer type) or full Night Sequence (adds audio cues — e.g. a Mass Murderer chainsaw sound plays even if his kill failed, leaking role presence). Repeat until a faction's win condition is met. Game can start at Day, Night, or Day(No-Lynch) (the common choice; also enables Night-1 jailing). After game end all players earn points (winners more), feeding unlockables/achievements; dead players meanwhile sit in graveyard chat and can gamble points on a Russian Roulette minigame.
game.setupSystem: Host picks a Variant: 'Classic' (preset: Mafioso/Consort/Citizen/Doctor/Sheriff only, no Last Wills/PMs/Trials), 'Clue' (no Last Wills, roles NOT revealed on death — Coroner becomes critical), 'Custom' (full editor: every role and option), or 'Save Slot' (reload a previously -save'd custom setup — how almost all real games are hosted; etiquette is to build the save alone offline because lobbies get impatient). The setup editor is a ROLE LIST of ~15 slots; each slot is either a SPECIFIC ROLE (e.g. Sheriff, Godfather) or a RANDOM CATEGORY slot that rolls a role from a pool: Town Government, Town Investigative, Town Protective, Town Killing, Town Power, Town Core, Town Random, Mafia Support, Mafia Deception, Mafia Killing, Mafia Random, Triad equivalents, Neutral Benign, Neutral Evil, Neutral Killing, Neutral Random, Any Random. Each category has per-role EXCLUDE toggles (e.g. 'Town Core: Exclude Citizen', 'Neutral Evil: Exclude Serial Killer'), and individual roles have 'Excluded from randoms' flags. Every role additionally has its own OPTION toggles that radically retune it, e.g.: Sheriff detects-Mafia/SK/Arsonist/Cult/MM toggles; Jailor 1/2/3/infinite executions; Vigilante shot count; Veteran alert count + ignores-invulnerability; Godfather immune-to-detection / roleblock-immune / kills-like-Mafioso; Witch 'can cause self-targets' and 'victim knows he is controlled'; Cultist conversion cooldown (1/2/3 nights) and 'immunity prevents conversion'; Survivor vest count; Mayor vote weight + 'cannot be healed'; Executioner 'becomes Jester upon failure' / 'target is always Town'; Citizen one-time bulletproof vest and 'wins 1v1 vs Mafia'. Game-level options: Day Type (4 voting modes), Night Type (Classic/Death Descriptions/Night Sequence), trial settings, day/night/discussion/trial lengths, Last Wills on/off, PMs on/off, Choose Names on/off, starting phase. The engine can EMULATE the setup (roll the randoms repeatedly) so hosts can check emergent probabilities. Constraint system: Unique roles (Godfather, Mayor, Marshall, Crier, Judge, Mason Leader, Dragon Head, Witch Doctor) max 1 alive; Mayor and Marshall mutually exclusive unless forced; 'powerless role' rules stop randoms rolling roles that would do nothing (e.g. Coroner only spawns from randoms if a Janitor/Incense Master or Clue variant is present; Framer/Forger won't roll with no Town to frame); an all-excluded Town Government slot defaults to Citizen. Players with enough points can -blacklist (up to 6) and -prefer (up to 3) roles to bias their own assignment. The most popular balance is 9 Town / 3 Mafia or Triad / 3 Neutral (1 Neutral Killing, 1 Neutral Evil, 1 Neutral Benign).

notableRoles.name: Citizen
notableRoles.mechanic: Vanilla; option for a one-night bulletproof vest and an option to win 1v1 ties vs Mafia/Triad

notableRoles.name: Sheriff
notableRoles.mechanic: Checks one player/night for alignment: 'member of the Mafia', 'Serial Killer', 'Arsonist', 'Cultist', 'Mass Murderer', or 'not suspicious' (per host detect toggles); fooled by Godfather detection immunity and Framer frames

notableRoles.name: Investigator
notableRoles.mechanic: Checks one player/night for their criminal record (crime list maps to role sets, e.g. 'Murder, Trespassing'); host option to instead reveal exact role

notableRoles.name: Detective
notableRoles.mechanic: Tracks one player/night, sees who they visited (sees FINAL post-swap visit)

notableRoles.name: Lookout
notableRoles.mechanic: Watches one player/night, sees everyone who visited them

notableRoles.name: Coroner
notableRoles.mechanic: Autopsies a dead body: learns exact role and night-by-night visit history; counter to Janitor and core of Clue variant

notableRoles.name: Spy
notableRoles.mechanic: Reads Mafia/Triad/Cult/Mason night chats anonymously (no speaker names); options to also see the Mafia kill target

notableRoles.name: Doctor
notableRoles.mechanic: Heals one player/night, negating one kill; options: knows if target attacked, prevents/detects Cult conversion; becomes Witch Doctor if converted (option)

notableRoles.name: Bodyguard
notableRoles.mechanic: Guards one player; if guarded player is attacked, attacker and Bodyguard BOTH die in a duel, target survives; at a Mass Murderer spree saves everyone and kills the MM

notableRoles.name: Escort
notableRoles.mechanic: Roleblocks one player/night, cancelling their action; some roles roleblock-immune; SK option 'kills roleblockers'

notableRoles.name: Bus Driver
notableRoles.mechanic: Swaps two players; every targeted action on one hits the other instead; can kill via redirection; chaotic dual-use protective/power role

notableRoles.name: Vigilante
notableRoles.mechanic: Night kill with host-limited shots (1-4 or unlimited); can't shoot N1; mislynches town when wrong ('Town Serial Killer')

notableRoles.name: Veteran
notableRoles.mechanic: Goes 'on alert' (limited count): automatically kills every visitor that night, optionally ignoring night immunity; roleblock-immune

notableRoles.name: Jailor
notableRoles.mechanic: During a day with no lynch, selects (-jail) a target to jail that night: target is roleblocked (ignores roleblock immunity), protected (not from Arsonist), talks with Jailor in anonymous jail chat, and may be EXECUTED (pierces all night immunity, can't be healed); host-limited executions (1/2/3/infinite)

notableRoles.name: Mayor
notableRoles.mechanic: Unique; reveals self with -vote for permanent extra votes (e.g. counts as 4); option: can no longer be healed after reveal

notableRoles.name: Marshall
notableRoles.mechanic: Unique; reveals self to trigger a group-lynch day: multiple lynches, no trials; mutually exclusive with Mayor

notableRoles.name: Crier
notableRoles.mechanic: Unique; speaks anonymously to the whole town at night (only night-talking Town role); can disrupt/expose a Judge

notableRoles.name: Mason / Mason Leader
notableRoles.mechanic: Masons share a night chat and know each other; Mason Leader (unique) recruits one Citizen per night (limited recruits), bludgeons any Cultist he targets, immune to Cult conversion; Mason can become Leader if Leader dies (option)

notableRoles.name: Godfather
notableRoles.mechanic: Unique faction leader; final say on the night kill (-notarget possible), options for night immunity, detection immunity (reads 'not suspicious'), roleblock immunity, and killing personally when no Mafioso lives

notableRoles.name: Mafioso
notableRoles.mechanic: Basic killer; Mafiosos vote/suggest kill targets, one random Mafioso carries out the chosen kill

notableRoles.name: Consigliere
notableRoles.mechanic: Mafia Investigator: checks crimes or exact role per settings

notableRoles.name: Consort
notableRoles.mechanic: Mafia Escort: roleblocks one player/night

notableRoles.name: Janitor
notableRoles.mechanic: Sanitizes a target: if they die that night their role and Last Will are hidden from the town

notableRoles.name: Framer
notableRoles.mechanic: Frames a player: Sheriff sees them as Mafia (or a living neutral killer), Investigator gets planted crimes

notableRoles.name: Disguiser
notableRoles.mechanic: Kills a player and steals their identity/name; own Last Will left on old body (option-dependent); the dead victim appears as the Disguiser

notableRoles.name: Blackmailer
notableRoles.mechanic: Silences a player for the next day: they cannot talk (or whisper/reveal as Mayor; a blackmailed jailed target cannot answer the Jailor)

notableRoles.name: Beguiler
notableRoles.mechanic: Hides behind a target at night: anything targeting the Beguiler is redirected to that target

notableRoles.name: Agent
notableRoles.mechanic: Combined Detective+Lookout on one target (sees who they visited and who visited them)

notableRoles.name: Kidnapper
notableRoles.mechanic: Mafia Jailor: jails+roleblocks after a no-lynch day, anonymous chat, may execute (jail also protects target from the Mafia kill)

roleCatalog.alignment: Triad (second scum faction; blue; mirror of Mafia)

notableRoles.name: Dragon Head
notableRoles.mechanic: = Godfather

notableRoles.name: Enforcer
notableRoles.mechanic: = Mafioso

notableRoles.name: Administrator
notableRoles.mechanic: = Consigliere

notableRoles.name: Liaison
notableRoles.mechanic: = Consort

notableRoles.name: Incense Master
notableRoles.mechanic: = Janitor

notableRoles.name: Forger
notableRoles.mechanic: = Framer

notableRoles.name: Informant
notableRoles.mechanic: = Disguiser

notableRoles.name: Silencer
notableRoles.mechanic: = Blackmailer

notableRoles.name: Deceiver
notableRoles.mechanic: = Beguiler

notableRoles.name: Vanguard
notableRoles.mechanic: = Agent

notableRoles.name: Interrogator
notableRoles.mechanic: = Kidnapper; only real faction difference: Triad wins ties over Mafia. Mafia and Triad can coexist in one setup as hostile rival factions with separate night chats; a Spy can't tell their kills apart

roleCatalog.alignment: Neutral Benign (own goals, can win with anyone)

notableRoles.name: Survivor
notableRoles.mechanic: Win = just survive to game end (wins alongside any faction); gets N bulletproof vests (usually 4) usable for night immunity

notableRoles.name: Jester
notableRoles.mechanic: Win = get LYNCHED (night death doesn't count); can 'annoy' a player at night (they're told a Jester visited); on lynch, option makes one random guilty voter commit grief suicide the next night

notableRoles.name: Executioner
notableRoles.mechanic: Win = see his game-assigned target lynched (option: target always Town); option: becomes a Jester if target dies at night; option: night invulnerable

notableRoles.name: Amnesiac
notableRoles.mechanic: Converts to (remembers) the role of any DEAD player in the graveyard, inheriting that role's win condition; options restrict becoming Town/Mafia/killing; immune to Witch control and roleblock

roleCatalog.alignment: Neutral Evil (win = survive and see Town lose; all win with the Cult)

notableRoles.name: Witch
notableRoles.mechanic: Controls one player/night, forcing their night action onto a target of the Witch's choice (can force self-targets per option); victim-knows-controlled option; can't control Amnesiacs/the dead-targeting; counts as a kill route via Veterans/killers; wins with Mafia/Triad/NK/Cult/other Witches

notableRoles.name: Auditor
notableRoles.mechanic: Converts one player/night: Town→Citizen, Mafia→Mafioso, Triad→Enforcer, non-immune Neutrals→Scumbag; cannot audit night-immune roles; targets are notified they were audited

notableRoles.name: Judge
notableRoles.mechanic: Unique; may 'call court' during the day: discussion stops, forced anonymous ballot, Judge speaks as 'Court' (everyone else 'Jury') and gets bonus votes — can single-handedly lynch late-game; also speaks anonymously at night (appears as a Crier)

notableRoles.name: Scumbag
notableRoles.mechanic: Vanilla survive-and-see-Town-lose role created only by an Auditor converting a Neutral; not host-selectable

notableRoles.name: Cultist
notableRoles.mechanic: CULT sub-faction: shared night chat, democratically votes one conversion per cooldown (1/2/3 nights); cannot convert Mafia/Triad; night immunity blocks conversion (option); Cult capped at 1/3 of original game size minus Mafia, regains a conversion per two dead Cultists; converted players keep their old appearance but join Cult chat; Mason Leader kills Cultists he visits

notableRoles.name: Witch Doctor
notableRoles.mechanic: Unique Cult support: 'heals' a player — if that player is attacked, they survive AND are converted to the Cult (limited saves); Cult win = everyone else dead or converted; Doctor/Witch converted by Cult become the Witch Doctor if none exists (options)

notableRoles.name: Elector (removed)
notableRoles.mechanic: Scrapped role: stole one player's vote and gave it to another at night

roleCatalog.alignment: Neutral Killing (subset of Neutral Evil; win = be last left standing; night-immune by default)

notableRoles.name: Serial Killer
notableRoles.mechanic: Kills one player/night; options: night invulnerable, kills roleblockers (Escort/Jailor who releases him dies), wins-ties-over-Arsonist

notableRoles.name: Arsonist
notableRoles.mechanic: Each night either DOUSES a target in gasoline or IGNITES all doused players at once (mass kill, option ignores healing immunity); can undouse self by idling; doused players may or may not be notified (option)

notableRoles.name: Mass Murderer
notableRoles.mechanic: Stages a killing spree at a target's house: kills the target (if home, i.e. took no action) and every visitor; 1-2 night cooldown after killing 2+; Bodyguard at the scene saves everyone and kills the MM; can target self to camp his own house

notableRoles.name: Electromaniac
notableRoles.mechanic: Charges up to two players/night; if any two charged players contact each other both die; visiting a charged player kills them instantly; pierces ALL protection and immunity

notableRoles.name: Poisoner
notableRoles.mechanic: (Later addition) Poisons a player who dies some days later unless a Doctor visits them; repeat visits accelerate death; different NK roles cannot win together, but duplicates of the same NK role can

chatMechanics: DAY CHAT: one public channel for all living players; the central deduction space. Dead players see everything but cannot speak to the living.

WHISPERS / PMs (-pm color/number msg, -r to reply): private content, but PUBLIC metadata — everyone is notified 'X is whispering to Y'. Host toggle; older versions let the Spy read PMs. Critical for role-claiming to a revealed Mayor/Marshall.

MAFIA NIGHT CHAT: all Mafia members talk privately each night and coordinate the kill via -target votes (Godfather has final say, -notarget possible). TRIAD has an identical separate chat; the two factions cannot hear each other.

CULT NIGHT CHAT: all Cultists + Witch Doctor talk at night and vote democratically on the conversion target (ties broken randomly). A Disguiser who steals a Cultist's identity does NOT get into Cult chat.
MASON NIGHT CHAT: Masons and Mason Leader talk privately at night (Town-aligned mirror of the Cult).

JAILOR CHAT: Jailor (or Kidnapper/Interrogator) converses one-on-one with his jailed prisoner; the Jailor's identity is anonymized as 'Jailor'. Quirk: two Jailors jailing the same target share one chat without knowing each other's identity. Blackmailed prisoners cannot reply.
SPY: reads Mafia/Triad/Cult/Mason night chats with speaker names hidden; option to see kill/conversion targets.

CRIER: broadcasts anonymously to the entire town at night ('the Crier says...'). JUDGE: also speaks anonymously at night (indistinguishable from a Crier) and during his 'court' day all non-Judge chat is anonymized as 'Jury'.
BLACKMAILER/SILENCER: target is mute the entire next day — cannot talk, and a blackmailed Mayor cannot reveal.

DEAD CHAT (graveyard): dead players chat freely among themselves, see all hidden info, and can play the Russian Roulette points minigame (-roulette/-join/-bet/-pull/-pass). No medium-style channel back to the living (that was Town of Salem's later addition).

LAST WILLS (-lw / -last will): up to 2 lines, editable any time while alive via a popup editor, revealed publicly on death (next dawn if night-killed, immediately if lynched). Anyone can re-read a dead player's will with -lw <number>. Convention: investigators log night results in shorthand ('N1: #7 (NS), N2: #5 (Mafia)'). Janitor/Incense Master cleaning hides role AND will; Clue variant disables wills entirely; host can disable wills.
DEATH NOTES (-dn msg): only non-Town killing roles (incl. Witch) may write one; it is displayed next to each victim they kill — used for taunts and disinformation.
MISC: -mute <player> client-side mute; -skip (50% of living skips day); -suicide (after day 3, kills self at night, used to dodge or to validate a Last Will posthumously).
winConditions: TOWN: lynch/kill every Mafia, Triad, Cultist, Neutral Killing and hostile Neutral Evil player. Town members all win together.

MAFIA: kill everyone who opposes them; effectively wins at parity — tiebreaker rules give Mafia the win when Mafia numbers >= Town numbers. Optional rule lets a lone Citizen beat the last Mafioso 1v1.
TRIAD: identical to Mafia, but wins ties OVER the Mafia (1v1 order: Triad > Mafia). When both factions are in a setup they must also eliminate each other.
CULT (Cultist + Witch Doctor): wins when every player is dead or converted — cannot win with Mafia/Triad or Neutral Killers, CAN win with other Neutral Benign/Evil roles.

NEUTRAL KILLING (SK/Arsonist/MM/Electromaniac/Poisoner): be the last faction standing; can win with Neutral Evil (except Cult) and Neutral Benign; different NK roles can never win together but duplicates of the same role can (2 SKs can co-win).

NEUTRAL EVIL non-killing (Witch/Judge/Auditor/Scumbag): 'survive and see the Town lose' — they ride along with whichever evil faction wins, and all of them also win with the Cult; they can also achieve rare solo wins.

NEUTRAL BENIGN: Survivor = simply alive at game end, stacks with any winner; Jester = gets lynched (instant personal win, + a guilty voter suicides); Executioner = his assigned target gets lynched while Exe lives (becomes Jester on failure, per option); Amnesiac = inherits the win condition of whatever graveyard role he remembers (or survives without converting).

DRAW/STALEMATE HANDLING: 'Three Days of Peace' — if nobody dies for 3 consecutive nights, day voting switches to anonymous ballot; persistent vote ties trigger re-votes until time expires, then a tiebreaker formula ends the game (Town wins if it outnumbers Mafia; Mafia wins at >= Town; Neutrals win if they outnumber Town; largest faction beats mixed Neutrals).

ONE-VERSUS-ONE AUTO-RESOLUTION: when the game reaches 1v1 at the start of a day it auto-concludes by priority: Arsonist > Serial Killer (option can flip SK over Arsonist) > Mass Murderer > Triad > Mafia (option: lone Citizen beats Mafia/Triad) > Cult > Witch/Judge/Auditor (win alongside the above) > Town > Executioner > Amnesiac > Survivor > Jester.
trickyMechanics: GLOBAL NIGHT RESOLUTION ORDER (published by the developer Dark Revenant, June 2011): 1) Jailor/Kidnapper detains target; 2) night chats open (Mafia/Mason/Cult/Jailor); 3) bulletproof vests applied; 4) TARGET MANIPULATION LOOP — Witch controls, then Bus Driver swaps, then roleblockers (Escort/Consort), and this Witch→BusDriver→Roleblocker cycle REPEATS a random number of times to settle 'complicated webs of events and paradoxes' (e.g. escort blocks escort blocking witch); 5) Framer frames, Arsonist douses/undouses, misc non-killing actions; 6) ALL KILLS RESOLVE SIMULTANEOUSLY but are reported in fixed order — Jailor execution, Vigilante, Mafioso/Godfather, Serial Killer, Arsonist ignition, Mass Murderer, Jester grief-suicide, Disguiser, leaver suicides — with Bodyguard duels, Bus Driver collision kills, and Witch-forced kills interleaved; being killed in an earlier step does NOT cancel your own queued kill (dead men's knives still land); 7) Janitor cleans; 8) investigations resolve (Sheriff, Investigator, Consigliere) — i.e. info roles see POST-kill state; 9) Disguiser assumes identity if his kill succeeded; 10) Mason Leader recruit; 11) Cult conversion last.

SIMULTANEOUS SUBMISSION: all players lock in actions during the timed night; nothing resolves until the night ends, then the deterministic pipeline above runs. Conflicting actions are settled purely by that priority order, not submission time.

REDIRECTION STACK: Bus Driver swaps redirect every targeted action including kills and heals (forcing Mafia to kill their own is a core play); Beguiler/Deceiver hide-behind redirects everything aimed at THEM onto their host; Witch redirects the victim's OWN action. Detective reports show the FINAL visit after all swaps. Witch-on-Witch is defined: a Witch's 'action target' is the person she controls, so controlling a Witch re-aims who that second Witch controls, not her victim's target.

ROLEBLOCK EDGE CASES: jail roleblocks even roleblock-immune roles (Veteran, Amnesiac, Godfather w/ immunity); Serial Killer option kills roleblockers (an Escort who blocks him, or a Jailor who jails-and-releases him, dies); Jailor's own execution can be roleblocked by an Escort/Consort; Jailor is hardcoded immune to Witch control (acknowledged bug).

PROTECTION/IMMUNITY LADDER: night immunity (Godfather, NK roles, vests) blocks normal kills; piercing effects: Jailor execute (ignores immunity AND healing), Veteran alert (option: ignores invulnerability), Electromaniac (pierces everything), Arsonist option burns through Doctor heals. Bodyguard intercept kills the attacker and himself, saving the target; at a Mass Murderer spree the Bodyguard saves all visitors and kills the MM. Doctor heal beats one kill; multiple simultaneous attacks overwhelm a single heal.

VISIT SEMANTICS: actions = 'visits'; Lookout/Detective/Agent/Vanguard observe visits; Veteran kills visitors; Mass Murderer kills everyone 'at the house' (a target who took an action is 'not home' and survives); non-visiting roles can still be FORCED to visit by a Witch (a witched Citizen will show up in Lookout reports and die to a Veteran); jailed targets never visit and are 'always home'; Jailor visits his captive only when executing (creates a documented MM corner case).

CONVERSION SYSTEMS (hardest to implement): Cult — democratic vote, cooldown 1-3 nights, cannot convert Mafia/Triad, night-immunity/vests block conversion (option), 1/3-of-original-players cap with refund of one conversion per two dead Cultists, Mason Leader insta-kills Cultists he targets and Masons are unconvertible, Doctor/Witch convert into the unique Witch Doctor, Witch Doctor 'heal-converts' attacked targets and may push past the cap, Doctor heal beats Witch Doctor heal on the same target; Auditor — converts Town→Citizen / Mafia→Mafioso / Triad→Enforcer / Neutral→Scumbag, blocked by night immunity; Amnesiac — converts himself to any graveyard role; Mason Leader — recruits Citizens only; Executioner→Jester on failed objective. Resolution order puts both recruit/convert steps dead last.

FACTION KILL DELEGATION: Mafiosos vote/suggest targets, a random living Mafioso performs the kill, Godfather overrides; with no Mafioso the Godfather kills personally only if the host option allows; non-killing Mafia can -target to direct an AFK killer; a leaver's role 'suicides' but their queued kill still resolves.

UNIQUE-ROLE & SPAWN CONSTRAINTS: only one Godfather/Mayor/Marshall/Crier/Judge/Mason-Leader/Witch-Doctor/Dragon-Head alive at a time; Mayor and Marshall are mutually exclusive via a shared uniqueness category; random slots must not roll 'powerless' roles (Coroner needs a Janitor/Clue context; Framer needs Town to frame; Mason Leader only spawns alongside Citizens/Cultists); an impossible random slot defaults to Citizen.

INFORMATION-MASKING INTERACTIONS: Janitor hides role+will of victims; Disguiser swaps identities (graveyard shows the wrong person); Framer corrupts Sheriff/Investigator reads; Godfather detection immunity reads 'not suspicious'; Death Descriptions / Night Sequence leak killer-type via flavor text and sounds (MM sound plays even on a failed spree); Coroner exists specifically to undo masking.

STALEMATE DETECTION: the engine itself enforces endgame — Three-Days-of-Peace ballot mode + numeric tiebreaker formula, and the 1v1 auto-resolution priority table — so the implementation needs faction-counting logic evaluated at the start of every day.
mvpRoleSet: Citizen — vanilla baseline; gives the role list flexible filler and teaches the 'power of the vote' core (add the 1-use vest option for spice).
Sheriff — the Town's alignment-check engine; the single most load-bearing info role and the anchor for Last-Will meta.
Investigator — second, fuzzier info channel (crime records) so claims can cross-check without making detection trivial.
Lookout — visit-based information; creates the visits/watch web that makes night actions legible and catches killers.
Doctor — the canonical protective; heal-vs-kill is the most fundamental night interaction to get right first.
Escort — Town roleblocker; introduces action-cancellation and the roleblock layer of the resolution order.
Jailor — SC2Mafia's signature role: day-selected jail, anonymous prisoner chat, immunity-piercing execution; generates the game's best moments and exercises chat + roleblock + kill systems at once.
Vigilante — Town kill with limited shots; high-drama misfires and the simplest 'Town can also kill' lever.
Mayor — one unique reveal role; the -vote reveal moment plus vote-weight mechanic is cheap to build and hugely fun.
Godfather — Mafia leader: night immunity + detection immunity + final kill say; teaches immunity and faction kill delegation.
Mafioso — kill executor and succession body for the Mafia (vote-the-target mechanic).
Consort — Mafia mirror of the Escort; WIFOM between Escort/Consort claims is classic and reuses the roleblock code.
Framer — one deception role so Sheriff results aren't gospel; minimal code (a flag on investigation results) for huge meta payoff.
Serial Killer — one Neutral Killing third threat; night-immune solo killer forces three-way tension and exercises last-man-standing win logic.
Jester — the beloved chaos role; trivial to implement (win-on-lynch + guilty-voter suicide) and instantly makes lynching decisions psychologically interesting.

(Optional 16th/swaps: Executioner or Survivor for a second benign neutral — both are near-free to implement; defer Witch, Bus Driver, Cult, Triad, Veteran, Mass Murderer, Disguiser to post-MVP since they drive most of the resolution-order complexity.)

Recommended MVP slot template (15p): Sheriff, Investigator, Lookout, Doctor, Escort, Jailor, Vigilante, Mayor, Citizen | Godfather, Mafioso, Consort or Framer | Serial Killer, Jester, Survivor/Executioner — matching the canonical 9 Town / 3 Mafia / 3 Neutral balance.
game.fullScopeNotes: Full SC2Mafia scope is roughly 60 roles: 20 Town (6 Government, 5-6 Investigative, 4 Protective, 4 Killing/Power overlapping, plus Spy and oddities like Stump (punishment role) and seasonal Caroler), 11 Mafia, 11 Triad (pure mirror of Mafia with renamed roles whose only mechanical difference is winning ties — cheap to add once Mafia exists, supports Mafia-vs-Triad three-way games with separate chats), ~15 Neutrals (4 Benign, 6+ non-killing Evil incl. the Cult conversion sub-faction and the Auditor-spawned Scumbag, 4-5 Killing incl. later additions Electromaniac and Poisoner, plus the scrapped Elector). Beyond roles, full scope includes: the four-variant host system (Classic/Clue/Custom/Save Slot) with save persistence and setup emulation/probability rolling; ~17 random-category slot types with per-role exclusion matrices; dozens of per-role option toggles that change role identity (this option system is the real configuration surface — every role page lists 3-8 toggles); 4 day/voting types and 3 night-reveal types with trial timer plumbing; Last Wills/Death Notes/PMs; unique-role and powerless-role spawn constraint solving; the full deterministic night-resolution pipeline with the repeated Witch/BusDriver/Roleblock cycle; stalemate machinery (Three Days of Peace, tiebreaker formula, 1v1 priority table); blackmail/silence states; conversion bookkeeping (Cult caps, Witch Doctor uniqueness, Auditor downgrades, Amnesiac remembering, Mason recruiting); meta-progression (points, achievements per-role win list via -alist, unlockable models/appendages, colored names, role blacklist/prefer weighting); lobby tooling (host repick voting, -default setup-of-the-day, kick-vote lists); and the graveyard Russian Roulette betting minigame. Historical note for synthesis: SC2Mafia (by Dark.Revenant) is the direct ancestor of Town of Salem — BlankMediaGames lifted the trial/defense/judgment loop, last wills, death notes, whispers, role-category randoms, and many role designs (Jailor, Veteran, Executioner, Jester, SK, Arsonist) nearly verbatim, so ToS docs are a usable secondary reference, but SC2Mafia is notably more permissive (free-text everything, host-configurable everything) and includes systems ToS dropped (Triad, Auditor/Judge/Marshall/Crier, Bus Driver chaos, court, multi-jailor chat). Primary sources: sc2mafia.fandom.com wiki pages — Game Guide, Hosting Guide, Mechanics (developer-confirmed night order), Commands, Last Will, Setups, all role/category pages (fetched via MediaWiki API; raw text cached under /tmp/sc2mafia/); supplemented by sc2mafia.com forum threads on Triad tie-wins and witch/jailor edge-case rulings.

options.name: Web tech: TypeScript + Electron (+ optional PixiJS) + steamworks.js
options.steamIntegration: steamworks.js (ceifa/steamworks.js): Rust-based N-API bindings, prebuilt binaries on npm, full TypeScript definitions, Electron/NW.js/Node support. Not archived; last push Apr 2026, 613 stars, 67 open issues, effectively single-maintainer (the 'not maintained' quote in its README refers to greenworks, the legacy alternative). Covers achievements, cloud, auth tickets, matchmaking/lobbies, workshop, overlay activation. KNOWN HARD LIMIT: Steam overlay does not work on macOS for Electron apps at all (electron/electron#42656, ceifa/steamworks.js#50) and only works on Windows with --in-process-gpu plus repaint caveats — architectural multi-process browser limitation, not fixable by config. Tauri alternative is immature: only tauri-plugin-hal-steamworks v0.0.4 on crates.io, and the Steam overlay cannot hook Tauri's system webview (tauri-apps/tauri#6196); Electron/NW.js are the only frameworks the established JS Steam bindings officially support (webgamedev.com/publishing/desktop).
pros: Maximum dev velocity for THIS dev: reuses TypeScript/Node/Postgres end-to-end; shared types/validation between client and game server (socket.io/tRPC/zod), hot reload, Chrome DevTools

Best-in-class UI tooling for a chat-heavy game: HTML/CSS/React (or Svelte/Solid) gives rich text, emoji, virtualized scrollback (react-virtuoso), tooltips, theming, accessibility — strictly better than any game-engine UI system for this genre

Proven shipping path: CrossCode (NW.js, 93% positive, 10k+ reviews) and shapez (Electron, Overwhelmingly Positive) shipped Win/macOS/Linux on Steam this way; gamedevjs.com and overactiongamestudio.com publish current Electron+steamworks.js pipelines

Strategic bonus unique to this route: same codebase can ship a free browser version to seed the multiplayer player base (Town of Salem itself started as a browser game); social deduction games live or die on concurrent players
Server stays 100% TypeScript/Node on his own Linux boxes — server-authoritative design needs no Steam networking at all (plain WebSockets), so the weakest parts of Steamworks bindings are irrelevant
electron-builder automates macOS signing/notarization (with known entitlements: disable-library-validation + allow-dyld-environment-variables required for the Steamworks dylib per Valve docs)
cons: Steam overlay broken on macOS, flaky on Windows — friend invites must flow through the Steam client launching the game with a connect arg rather than Shift+Tab; some players notice and complain

Electron macOS notarization/hardened-runtime is a documented pain (electron-builder issues #3989/#4040: every nested binary must be signed, entitlements-inherit required) — solvable, well-trodden, but a real day or two of yak-shaving
~250 MB download and 'it's Electron' perception/memory overhead; mostly cosmetic for this genre
steamworks.js bus factor: one maintainer, 67 open issues; mitigations exist (forks like ai-zen/steamworks.js, or raw steamworks-rs via a small native module)
If the game later grows real-time gameplay (animations beyond CSS/PixiJS, particles, shaders), engine features must be hand-assembled from npm parts
No engine-experience résumé value; future console ports would require a rewrite (Steam-only plan makes this moot for now)

options.name: Godot 4 + GDScript + GodotSteam
options.steamIntegration: GodotSteam is the strongest open-source Steamworks binding of any engine: GDExtension 4.19.1 released 2026-05-29 already tracking Steamworks SDK 1.64 (released ~2 weeks prior), supports Windows/Linux/macOS, drop-in via Asset Library, includes auto-update checker. Active development moved from GitHub (archived 2026-05-23) to Codeberg (codeberg.org/godotsteam/godotsteam) — a hosting move, not abandonment; godotsteam.com has dedicated tutorials including Mac export. Near-complete Steamworks API coverage.
pros: Free, MIT-licensed, no revenue caps, no company risk of Unity-style license whiplash

Control-node UI system is the best among real game engines for menus/lists/themes; RichTextLabel has BBCode, its own scrollbar, append_text() incremental parsing and a Threaded mode for chat logs (docs.godotengine.org BBCode guide explicitly discusses multiplayer chat, including sanitizing user BBCode injection)
macOS export is first-class: export dialog has built-in codesign + notarization integration including rcodesign, which signs/notarizes from Linux/Windows without a Mac (godotengine PR #64207)
Server can stay TypeScript/Node: Godot's WebSocketPeer client talks to his existing stack, so only the client is 'new territory'
GDScript is a small Python-like language — days, not months, for a strong TS dev; enormous tutorial ecosystem; lightweight editor, fast iteration
Future-proof: if the game grows animations/minigames/juice, the engine absorbs it; Linux export trivially covers Steam Deck
cons: Whole-engine learning curve (scenes, nodes, signals, themes) before first pixel of real product — weeks of ramp-up a web stack wouldn't need
Chat UI is achievable but clunkier than DOM: RichTextLabel stutters on thousands-of-lines logs without the documented workarounds; no CSS, no virtualized-list library, theming system is its own skill
GDScript is dynamically typed and tooling (refactors, LSP) is weaker than TypeScript's; code can't be shared with the Node server — game rules logic gets duplicated or moved fully server-side
No browser-demo synergy with a native-feeling codebase (Godot web export exists but is heavy and C#/web export still unsupported)
Asset-store ecosystem smaller than Unity's, though largely irrelevant for a UI-first game

options.name: Godot 4 + C# (.NET) + GodotSteam C# bindings
options.steamIntegration: Same excellent GodotSteam core, but the C# layer lags: LauraWebdev/GodotSteam_CSharpBindings targets GodotSteam 4.6.1 / Godot 4.4+ and hasn't tracked GodotSteam 4.11+ — a community fork (craethke/GodotSteam_CSharpBindings) carries updated bindings. Workaround: call the GDExtension directly from C# via Godot's cross-language Call() per godotsteam.com/tutorials/c-sharp (works but loses typed API). steam-multiplayer-peer-csharp exists for Steam transport but is irrelevant given his own servers.
pros: C# is statically typed and closer to TypeScript ergonomics than GDScript; Rider/VS tooling is excellent
All Godot UI/export strengths from the GDScript option apply
Larger transferable-skill payoff (C# also unlocks Unity/MonoGame later)
cons: Steam bindings are the weakest link: official-ish C# bindings version-lag the rapidly-updated GodotSteam, forcing a fork or untyped Call() interop — ongoing friction for the project's most Steam-critical dependency
C# is still a new language for this dev (async model, .NET project system) on top of the engine learning curve
Godot's C# path has historically trailed GDScript in docs/tutorials and platform support (no web export), so community answers often need translation from GDScript
No code sharing with the Node server, same as GDScript

options.name: Unity 6 + Steamworks.NET (or Facepunch.Steamworks)
options.steamIntegration: Most mature Steam ecosystem of any engine. Steamworks.NET: faithful 1:1 wrapper of Valve's C++ API, decades of community guidance apply directly, broad third-party tooling (Heathen's Toolkit at kb.heathen.group/steam). Facepunch.Steamworks: idiomatic C# re-interpretation, shorter code, but diverges from Valve docs and tooling, maintenance historically spottier. Known macOS notarization recipes exist (Steamworks.NET issue #305, yemi.me Unity-Steam-macOS guide). Either binding fully covers auth/achievements/rich presence.
pros: Deepest asset store and largest community; an answer exists for everything
Steamworks.NET is the de-facto industry standard binding; lowest Steam-integration risk of all options
Town of Salem 2 itself is a Unity game — direct genre precedent

Runtime Fee cancelled (Sep 2024); Unity Personal free to $200k revenue/funding, splash screen optional in Unity 6 — licensing risk for a solo dev is currently low (unity.com/blog/unity-is-canceling-the-runtime-fee)
cons: UI is the project's core and Unity's UI story is split: UI Toolkit is the recommended modern path for chat/data-heavy UIs but still has documented runtime gaps in 2025 — scroll-view behavior pain, no built-in runtime tooltips or drag-drop (Angry Shark Studio 2025 guide, Unity UI Toolkit status threads); uGUI is mature but verbose and dated, with TextMeshPro confined to uGUI
Heaviest learning curve here: large opaque editor, C# (new language), prefab/serialization model, slow domain reloads — worst dev-velocity match for a web-native solo dev
Closed source; company strategy risk (post-runtime-fee trust damage, 5% Pro price rise Jan 2026) even though Personal terms are fine today
Engine is overkill: 3D-capable runtime, longer build times, larger baseline complexity for a game that is lobby + chat + timers
No code sharing with Node server; no browser-demo synergy comparable to web stack

options.name: Others (brief): Bevy, MonoGame, Defold, Ebitengine
options.steamIntegration: Bevy: steamworks-rs / bevy_steamworks exist and Rust bindings are solid, but engine UI is the blocker. Defold: official, actively maintained extension-steam with hand-written Lua bindings (defold.com/extension-steam), macOS dev requires copying Steam dylibs to /usr/local/lib for editor runs. MonoGame: uses Steamworks.NET directly — binding fine, everything else manual. Ebitengine: official Steam shipping guide (ebitengine.org/en/documents/steam.html) but go-steamworks 'has not yet implemented most of the API'; macOS requires manual .app assembly, notarization, and ditto-zip quirks; known Steam-launch hang and overlay issues (ebiten #3181, #3338).
pros: Defold is the most credible of the four: tiny runtime, official Steam extension, good 2D, free with no revenue share
Bevy 0.18 (Mar 2026) shows real momentum — first editor preview, bevy_feathers widgets — for anyone already in Rust
MonoGame and Ebitengine offer total code-level control with no engine lock-in
cons: Bevy: Rust learning curve is the steepest possible jump from TypeScript; bevy_ui remains low-level for a rich chat UI (community consensus still patches it with egui/sickle_ui) — wrong tool for a UI-first game in 2026
MonoGame: no UI system at all — chat, scrollbars, tooltips, text layout all hand-rolled or via third-party libs; macOS packaging fully manual; worst-case velocity
Defold: gui system is built for HUDs, not thousand-line rich-text chat scrollback; Lua + smaller community; ecosystem thin for this genre
Ebitengine: minimal immediate-mode drawing, Go UI ecosystem nearly empty, go-steamworks API coverage explicitly incomplete, fiddly macOS/Steam quirks

stack.recommendation: Build it in web tech: TypeScript client (React or Svelte; add PixiJS only if/when you want canvas-rendered flair) wrapped in Electron with steamworks.js, talking WebSockets to your own Node/Postgres servers. Runner-up if you want to bet on an engine anyway: Godot 4 with GDScript + GodotSteam, keeping the server in Node.
stack.reasoning: Honest answer to the framing question: no, a game engine is not necessary for this game, and for this developer it is actively the slower path. A social deduction game is a lobby, a chat scrollback, vote/role panels, timers, and tooltips — exactly the workload DOM/CSS was built for and exactly where every game engine's UI system is the weak point (Godot's RichTextLabel needs documented workarounds for large chat logs; Unity's UI Toolkit still lacks runtime tooltips/drag-drop and has scroll-view pain per 2025 status threads; MonoGame/Ebitengine/Bevy have effectively nothing). Meanwhile the dev's existing TypeScript/Node/Postgres skills transfer 1:1, including shared types between client and authoritative server — the single biggest correctness lever in a protocol-heavy deduction game. The route is commercially proven on Steam for Win+macOS (CrossCode via NW.js, shapez via Electron), steamworks.js is alive (pushed Apr 2026, prebuilt npm binaries, TS definitions), and Steam-side needs are thin anyway because game networking runs on his own servers — Steamworks is only auth tickets, achievements, rich presence, and presence-based invites. The unique strategic kicker: the same codebase ships a free browser build to seed the player base, which is existential for an online social deduction game (Town of Salem itself grew from a browser game). The two real costs are known and bounded: (1) Steam overlay does not work on macOS for Electron and is flaky on Windows — route invites through the Steam client launch flow instead; (2) Electron macOS signing/notarization yak-shaving — solved by electron-builder plus Valve's documented entitlements (disable-library-validation, allow-dyld-environment-variables). Tauri is rejected for Steam specifically: the overlay cannot hook its system webview, the only Steamworks plugin is v0.0.4, and macOS WKWebView adds rendering inconsistency — Electron is the web wrapper that works. If the dev prefers insurance for a more game-like future (animated night phases, minigames, juice), Godot 4 GDScript + GodotSteam is a strong 7/10: best-in-engine-class UI nodes, the most actively maintained Steam binding in any engine (4.19.1, May 2026, now on Codeberg), built-in macOS signing/notarization including Mac-less rcodesign, and the server still stays in Node via WebSockets. Avoid the Godot C# path (C# Steam bindings version-lag GodotSteam, forcing forks or untyped interop). Unity (5/10) is the safe-but-slow industrial choice whose strengths (3D, asset store, console ports) this project doesn't use, bought with the steepest ramp for a web-native solo dev. Key sources: codeberg.org/godotsteam/godotsteam (releases), godotsteam.com/blog, github.com/ceifa/steamworks.js + GitHub API (activity), electron/electron#42656 and ceifa/steamworks.js#50 (macOS overlay), tauri-apps/tauri#6196 (Tauri overlay), docs.godotengine.org (RichTextLabel/BBCode, exporting_for_macos + PR #64207 rcodesign), unity.com/blog/unity-is-canceling-the-runtime-fee, angry-shark-studio.com UI Toolkit vs UGUI 2025, partner.steamgames.com macOS requirements + steamcommunity Steamworks announcement (64-bit/notarization, entitlements), defold.com/extension-steam, ebitengine.org/en/documents/steam.html, strayspark.studio Bevy-2026 and thisweekinbevy (Bevy 0.18 maturity), LauraWebdev/GodotSteam_CSharpBindings + craethke fork (C# lag), wiki.facepunch.com/steamworks and kb.heathen.group/steam (Steamworks.NET vs Facepunch).

net.whyServerAuthoritative: In a hidden-information game the only working defense is to NEVER transmit the secret. Anti-cheat, obfuscation, and encryption all fail because the cheat runs on the client, which must be able to decrypt whatever it receives — any data delivered to the client is readable via packet inspection or memory reads. Two case studies prove both directions: (1) Among Us used host-authoritative P2P-style architecture; role assignment happened on the host device, and clients received enough state that 'role reveal' / ESP mod menus were trivial and 'virtually undetectable' because they were pure client-side information reads. The 2020 cheating wave forced Innersloth into emergency server-side work (sources: pcgamer.com/of-course-there-are-already-among-us-cheaters/, burgercheats.com mod-menu listings, screenrant.com vent-hack coverage). (2) Town of Salem kept roles server-side: community/dev discussions confirm role-view 'hacks' don't work precisely because 'the client doesn't know the other player's roles' — but players did experiment with packet readers, so anything that IS sent is compromised (steamcommunity.com/app/334230 discussions threads on role-view hacks). Design rule: per-client need-to-know filtering at the serialization layer. Each client receives only: its own role/abilities, public game events (deaths, vote tallies as revealed by rules), chat channels it belongs to, and information its role has legitimately learned (e.g., investigator results). Night actions of other players are never echoed; faction chat is routed server-side only to faction members; vote/night resolution happens entirely server-side from queued intents. Subtle leaks to also close: side channels — if mafia clients receive extra messages or larger payloads at night than town clients, packet-size/timing analysis leaks faction; unify or pad per-phase message patterns. Also never embed the full role list in lobby payloads, never send 'you were targeted but protected' details beyond what rules reveal, and strip secrets from spectator and post-game data until game end. Academic backing: arxiv.org/pdf/2501.10881 (Addressing Network Packet-based Cheats in Multiplayer Games) treats packet-based hidden-info cheats as an architectural problem, not a detection problem.
net.architecture: Two-tier split. TIER 1 — stateless lobby/matchmaking/auth service (plain HTTP/REST, horizontally scalable, no game state): handles login, party/queue, leaderboards reads, and issues a short-lived signed token {accountId, roomId} that admits the client to a specific game room. Also keeps a player→active-room registry so a restarted client can rediscover its in-progress game. TIER 2 — per-game room: one in-memory authoritative state machine instance per match (Colyseus 'Room' maps 1:1 to this; or a plain class in a Node process — at 50-500 CCU all rooms fit in one process). State machine phases: LOBBY → ROLE_ASSIGNMENT (single server-side seeded RNG; seed stored for audit/replay) → DAY_DISCUSSION → NOMINATION → TRIAL → VERDICT_VOTE → NIGHT (action queue collection) → NIGHT_RESOLUTION → check win → loop or GAME_OVER. Phase timers live server-side; on expiry the machine auto-transitions and applies defaults (abstain, no action) so a stalled/disconnected client can never block the game (pattern per mplgaming.com/server-authoritative-games/ and techtidesolutions.com/blog/game-server-architecture-basics/). NIGHT_RESOLUTION must be deterministic: collect all submitted intents into a queue during the night phase, validate each (alive? correct role? legal target? not roleblocked?), then resolve in a fixed published priority order (transports/roleblocks → protections → kills → investigations/info roles), producing an event list; this makes outcomes reproducible from (seed, intents) and enables replays and dispute audits. Message flow: client sends INTENTS only ({type:'vote', target}, {type:'night_action', target}, {type:'chat', channel, text}) → server validates against role+phase+alive status → mutates authoritative state → emits per-client FILTERED views (Colyseus StateView / boardgame.io playerView pattern: docs.colyseus.io/state/view, github.com/boardgameio/boardgame.io secret-state.md). Chat is just another server-routed channel: day chat broadcast to alive players, mafia chat only to mafia members, dead chat only to dead, whispers per game rules. Persistence boundary: live state in memory; append-only event log per match (for crash recovery, replays, ELO recompute, moderation evidence); transactional Postgres write of results at game end. Crash recovery via periodic snapshot or event-log replay is a nice-to-have at this scale, not a launch blocker.

transportOptions.name: Plain WebSockets (Node ws/uWebSockets.js, or Go)
transportOptions.verdict: CORRECT CHOICE. A Mafia-style game is turn-based + chat: low message rate, no latency sensitivity below ~200ms, and TCP head-of-line blocking is irrelevant — exactly the profile where reliable ordered WebSocket transport is recommended (blog.algomaster.io/p/websocket-use-cases-system-design, techtidesolutions.com game-server-architecture-basics). One Node process trivially holds 500 concurrent sockets. TLS via Caddy/nginx reverse proxy. Node fits the dev's TypeScript profile better than Go here; Go buys nothing at this scale.

transportOptions.name: Socket.IO on top of WebSockets
transportOptions.verdict: ACCEPTABLE. Adds rooms primitive (maps neatly to game/faction/dead chat channels), acks, auto-reconnect, and HTTP long-poll fallback. Costs: protocol overhead, and its room broadcast model still requires you to build the per-client state filtering yourself. The Redis adapter is only needed when scaling past one node — not needed at 500 CCU (socket.io/docs/v4/redis-adapter/, ably.com/topic/scaling-socketio). Reasonable DIY base, but Colyseus supersedes it for this genre.

transportOptions.name: Steam networking / Steam Datagram Relay (SDR)
transportOptions.verdict: DEFER UNTIL A STEAM RELEASE, AND ONLY AS TRANSPORT. SDR relays traffic over Valve's backbone: hides server and player IPs, gives DoS protection, encrypted+authenticated, free if the game ships on Steam (partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/multiplayer/steamdatagramrelay, github.com/ValveSoftware/GameNetworkingSockets). But it is a transport layer into your own authoritative server — it does not change the authority model, requires Steamworks SDK integration and a matchmaking service issuing auth tickets, and is pointless for a web-first launch. If/when shipping on Steam, route Steam clients through SDR into the same room servers; web clients keep WebSockets.

transportOptions.name: Peer-to-peer
transportOptions.verdict: NEVER ACCEPTABLE FOR THIS GENRE. Three independent disqualifiers: (1) hidden information — some peer must know all roles to arbitrate night resolution; whoever that is can cheat undetectably. This is exactly the Among Us host-authority failure: host-side role assignment enabled always-impostor mods and role-reveal ESP (pcgamer.com, screenrant.com). (2) IP exposure — peers learn each other's IPs, enabling DDoS/doxxing of players, uniquely toxic in a game whose core loop is accusing people. SDR exists largely to solve this for games that DO need P2P. (3) No trustworthy arbiter — votes, timers, and RNG can be manipulated by the host; host migration on rage-quit is unsolved pain. The bandwidth savings P2P offers are meaningless for a text game. There is no configuration in which P2P is acceptable here.

offTheShelf.name: Colyseus
offTheShelf.verdict: BEST FIT — recommended. Open-source (MIT) Node/TypeScript authoritative multiplayer framework; Room abstraction maps 1:1 to a Mafia game; built-in matchmaking, room lifecycle, and binary delta state sync (colyseus.io, github.com/colyseus/colyseus). Critically for hidden information: StateView (v0.16+, replacing the old @filter decorators) provides per-client state filtering — @view()-tagged fields are only serialized to clients whose StateView includes them, explicitly designed for 'private fields' and 'team-owned data' (docs.colyseus.io/state/view, colyseus.io/blog/colyseus-016-is-here/). Built-in allowReconnection() with private per-client reconnection tokens (hardened after a sessionId-impersonation vuln, github.com/colyseus/colyseus/issues/354). Self-hosts on any Linux box; single process fine to ~thousands CCU; Redis-backed scaling exists when needed. Caveats: StateView not optimized for huge datasets (irrelevant for 15-player rooms); persistence/accounts are your own (good — dev wants Postgres); double-check that nothing secret sits outside view-filtered fields.

offTheShelf.name: Nakama (Heroic Labs)
offTheShelf.verdict: CAPABLE BUT MISMATCHED. Apache-2 open-source Go server with batteries included: auth, friends, chat channels, leaderboards, matchmaking, authoritative match handlers in Go/Lua/TS runtime (github.com/heroiclabs/nakama). Friction for this dev: officially requires CockroachDB (Postgres only 'unofficially, dev environments only' per heroiclabs.com docs — though many run Postgres in prod anyway), authoritative match logic lives in Nakama's embedded runtime rather than a normal Node codebase, and the learning curve is widely reported as steep (saashub.com comparison). Self-hosts for ~$10/mo (snopekgames.com tutorial). Choose it only if the built-in social features (friends/chat/leaderboards) outweigh writing them yourself; per-client hidden-state filtering is still hand-rolled inside match handlers.

offTheShelf.name: Hathora
offTheShelf.verdict: ELIMINATED — SERVICE SHUT DOWN. Hathora announced on 2026-03-04 that its game server hosting platform shuts down 2026-05-05; the company pivoted to AI inference infrastructure (team joined Fireworks AI). Verified via gameye.com/gameye-vs-hathora/. Do not build on it. Its niche (per-room container orchestration, Edgegap/Gameye as successors) is overkill for 50-500 CCU anyway — that's one VPS.

offTheShelf.name: PlayFab (Microsoft)
offTheShelf.verdict: WRONG SHAPE FOR THIS DEV. Mature BaaS (since 2014): identity, economy, matchmaking, lobby, Party voice/chat; Standard/Premium tiers with $400/$8,000 of included usage meters then pay-as-you-go; dev mode capped at 1,000 lifetime accounts (playfab.com/pricing, learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/playfab/pricing). But: no self-hosting (hard conflict with this dev's profile), Azure/C#-flavored ecosystem, usage-metered lock-in, and the actual game room logic still has to run on your own/Azure servers — PlayFab solves the parts (accounts, stats) this dev already does comfortably in Postgres. Skip.

offTheShelf.name: Raw Socket.IO (DIY)
offTheShelf.verdict: VIABLE FALLBACK. Gives transport, rooms, acks, reconnect; you hand-roll room lifecycle, state machine, per-client filtered serialization, reconnection tokens, and matchmaking — i.e., you rebuild ~60% of Colyseus. Defensible if the dev wants zero framework magic and full control; otherwise Colyseus is the same stack with the hard parts done and audited (socket.io docs, dev.to/sauravmh/building-a-multiplayer-game-using-websockets-1n63).

offTheShelf.name: boardgame.io (bonus reference)
offTheShelf.verdict: PATTERN DONOR, NOT A PLATFORM. Its playerView / PlayerView.STRIP_SECRETS is the canonical open-source implementation of server-side secret stripping for turn-based games (github.com/boardgameio/boardgame.io secret-state.md) — worth reading even if not adopted. Maintenance is sleepy and its multiplayer server is less production-hardened; note its issue #399 (secrets leaking via ctx._undo/_initial) as a cautionary tale: secrets leak through ANY unfiltered side path, not just main state.

net.persistence: Postgres for everything durable (matches dev profile; no reason for anything else at this scale). Live game state stays in room memory — DB is for identity, history, and moderation. Schema-level sketch: accounts(id, email, auth_provider+provider_id or password_hash, display_name, created_at, last_login); sessions(refresh tokens, device info); player_stats(account_id, mode, rating, rating_deviation, games_played, wins; consider per-role/per-faction win-rate columns or a side table) — prefer Glicko-2 over vanilla Elo for a multiplayer team game (rating deviation handles sparse play; compute team-vs-team expected outcome per faction); matches(id, mode, started_at, ended_at, settings_json, winner_faction, rng_seed); match_players(match_id, account_id, seat, role, faction, outcome, rating_before, rating_after, left_early bool); match_events(match_id, seq, ts, type, payload JSONB, append-only) — this event log is triple-duty: replays, deterministic ELO/result recomputation, and moderation evidence; chat_messages either inside match_events or its own table (account_id, match_id, channel, text, ts) with a retention policy column/partitioning by month for cheap deletion; reports(id, reporter_id, reported_id, match_id, category, message_refs, free_text, status, resolution, resolved_by, created_at/resolved_at); sanctions(id, account_id, type[mute|ban|chat_ban], scope, reason, issuer_id, created_at, expires_at NULL=permanent) — checked at login and room-join; enforce mutes server-side in the chat path. Ranked queue can live in-process or Redis, but at 500 CCU an in-memory queue with Postgres write-through is fine; Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY covers cross-service pokes. Write match results in one transaction at game end (matches + match_players + rating updates). GDPR hook: account deletion anonymizes account row and match_players linkage but keeps aggregate/match integrity (replace with tombstone id).
net.hostingCosts: Cheap — this genre is text-plus-timers. 500 CCU ≈ ~35-50 concurrent rooms; per-client traffic is well under 1 KB/s with bursts at phase changes; a single Node process on 2 vCPU handles it with headroom. Realistic self-host stack (fits dev's existing Linux habits): 1× Hetzner CPX21/CCX13-class VPS (2-4 vCPU, 4-8 GB) for lobby+rooms: €8-15/mo (hetzner.com/cloud — entry instances from €3.49; 300-500 Mbit and ~20 TB traffic included, far beyond need); Postgres on the same box or a second small VPS: €0-10/mo; backups/object storage: €1-5/mo; TLS free (Let's Encrypt/Caddy); Cloudflare free tier in front of the lobby HTTP API for basic DDoS posture (game WebSocket connects direct or via proxied hostname). Total: roughly €15-40/mo (~$20-50). Comfort ceiling with managed Postgres (DO/Supabase ~$15-25/mo), a staging box, and uptime monitoring: $50-100/mo. At 50 CCU it's one $5-8 VPS. Per-room orchestration platforms are unjustified at this scale (and Hathora, the obvious one, shut down May 2026; Edgegap-style pricing ~$0.00115/min/vCPU only makes sense for latency-sensitive global session games). Cost only inflects past ~5-10k CCU, when you'd shard rooms across processes/boxes — a process-per-shard model the room architecture already permits. The dev's own hardware (existing fleet) could host this at ~$0 marginal, but a rented VPS gives clean IP reputation and keeps player traffic off the home/office network.
net.reconnection: Disconnects are routine (mobile networks, tab closes) and in this genre a disconnect must neither forfeit the game nor leak anything. Pattern (Colyseus has it built-in; replicate if DIY): (1) On socket drop, keep the player's seat and mark them 'disconnected' with a grace window — 60-120s or until current phase end, whichever is longer; other players see only a connectivity badge. (2) Reconnection auth uses a PRIVATE per-session reconnection token issued at join and ROTATED on every reconnect — Colyseus moved to this after a real vulnerability where knowing a victim's sessionId+roomId let an attacker reconnect as them and act on their behalf (github.com/colyseus/colyseus/issues/354). If hand-rolling: token is secret, single-use, bound to accountId+roomId. (3) On resume, the server sends a FULL fresh filtered snapshot for that client (their role, everything their role has learned, vote state, chat history for channels they belong to, current phase + remaining timer) — never trust or diff against the client's stale state; chat backfill bounded to the current match. (4) The stateless lobby keeps player→active-room mapping, so a fully restarted client can ask 'am I in a game?' and rejoin after app restart, not just socket blips. (5) Timer policy: phase timers never pause for disconnects; on expiry the state machine applies defaults (abstain, no night action) — the game always advances. (6) Abandonment policy for ranked: Colyseus allowReconnection('manual') supports custom logic like 'reject if player missed >2 rounds' (0-15-x.docs.colyseus.io/server/room/); convert to abandon + loss + escalating queue penalty after N missed phases. (7) Heartbeat ping/pong to detect half-open TCP promptly. Socket.IO's auto-reconnect handles transport retry but NOT identity/state resume — the token+snapshot layer is yours regardless of transport.
net.moderation: Minimum viable set for launch (social deduction chat is high-toxicity by construction — accusation is the core loop): (1) REPORTS: in-game report attached to match_id + specific message/event refs, with category picklist + free text. Shape it DSA Article 16-style from day one since EU users are likely: user-accessible flagging with substantiated reason and exact content location; store the report; notify both reporter and affected user of the decision; target ~72h human-review turnaround; maintain a monitored human contact point (blog.promise.legal/eu-digital-services-act-game-studios/, ggwp.com/the-digital-services-act/). Because the server logged the authoritative match_events stream, every report comes with verifiable evidence — no client screenshots needed. (2) MUTES/SANCTIONS: enforced server-side in the chat path (drop at server; never trust client-side hiding); sanctions table drives mute/chat-ban/account-ban checks at login and room-join; escalating durations; ban appeals path recommended (DSA pressure on unexplained bans is increasing — esportslegal.news 2025 coverage of gaming bans under DSA). (3) PROFANITY FILTER: server-side pass on every message before broadcast; use a maintained evasion-aware library (e.g., 'obscenity' on npm handles leetspeak/spacing tricks) rather than a naive regex list; launch policy: mask matches + keep report path, optionally let users toggle display filtering client-side — but the canonical stored log keeps the original for moderation. (4) LOG RETENTION (GDPR-ish): chat logs tied to accounts are personal data (gdpreu.org gaming-harassment analysis). No fixed statutory period — retention must match stated purpose (EDPB Guidelines 3/2025 on DSA/GDPR interplay). Practical policy: 30-90 days hot retention of chat/match logs for moderation purposes; logs referenced by open reports or active sanctions are retained until resolution + appeal window; then delete or anonymize; document this in the privacy policy; support access/export/erasure requests; partition chat tables by month so deletion is a DROP, not a scan. Defer to post-launch: ML toxicity scoring, voice, trust-score matchmaking.
net.recommendation: Build server-authoritative from line one: Colyseus (Node/TypeScript) self-hosted on a single Hetzner-class Linux VPS, plain WebSockets behind Caddy/nginx TLS, stateless HTTP lobby/auth service issuing signed room tokens, one Colyseus Room per match running an explicit phase state machine with server-side timers, queued night intents, and deterministic seeded resolution. Use StateView per-client filtering so secret roles, night actions, and faction chat are never serialized to unauthorized clients — this single architectural choice is what killed role-reveal cheats in Town of Salem and what Among Us lacked. Postgres for accounts, Glicko-2 ratings, match history (append-only match_events JSONB log), reports, and sanctions. Reconnection via Colyseus allowReconnection with private rotated tokens + full filtered snapshot on resume; phase timers never pause. Launch moderation: server-side mutes, evasion-aware profanity masking ('obscenity'), DSA-style report queue with 30-90 day log retention. Rejected: P2P (categorically — hidden info + IP exposure + no arbiter), Hathora (shut down 2026-05-05), PlayFab (no self-host, lock-in, wrong stack), Nakama (CockroachDB/Go runtime friction; only reconsider if built-in friends/chat/leaderboards become must-haves), raw Socket.IO (viable but rebuilds Colyseus by hand). Add Steam Datagram Relay later only as an additional transport into the same authoritative rooms if shipping on Steam (free, hides IPs, DDoS protection). Expected cost: ~$20-50/mo through 500 CCU; the architecture shards by room/process when growth demands it. Key sources: docs.colyseus.io/state/view; colyseus.io/blog/colyseus-016-is-here/; github.com/colyseus/colyseus/issues/354; steamcommunity.com/app/334230 role-hack threads; pcgamer.com Among Us cheaters; partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/multiplayer/steamdatagramrelay; github.com/heroiclabs/nakama; gameye.com/gameye-vs-hathora/ (shutdown); playfab.com/pricing; hetzner.com/cloud; github.com/boardgameio/boardgame.io secret-state docs; blog.promise.legal/eu-digital-services-act-game-studios/; edpb.europa.eu Guidelines 3/2025.

shippingSteps: Create a Steamworks partner account at partner.steamgames.com/steamdirect: requires a Steam account that has spent at least $5, legal entity/individual info, US tax interview (W-8BEN for non-US individuals -- relevant since user appears Japan-based), banking details for payouts, and identity verification. Onboarding paperwork typically clears in 1-3 days. (Source: https://partner.steamgames.com/steamdirect)

Pay the Steam Direct fee: $100 USD per app, non-refundable but recoupable once the app reaches $1,000 Adjusted Gross Revenue (store + in-app). (Source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/appfee)

Hard timing constraints baked into Steam Direct: you cannot release until 30 days after paying the app fee, AND your 'Coming Soon' store page must be publicly visible for at least 2 weeks before launch. Plan ~30 days minimum from signup to earliest possible release. (Sources: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/appfee, https://ziva.sh/blogs/publish-game-steam)

Build the store page: name, description, capsule art in all required sizes, at least 5 screenshots, trailer, tags, pricing, content survey. Submit the store page for Valve review -- typically 3-5 business days; rejections (usually for capsule art or missing assets) restart the cycle. Once approved, set it live as 'Coming Soon' to start the 2-week clock and accumulate wishlists. (Sources: https://partner.steamgames.com/steamdirect, https://www.summerengine.com/blog/how-to-publish-game-on-steam)

Upload builds via SteamPipe: use the SDK's ContentBuilder (steamcmd + run_app_build), with an app_build_[AppID].vdf referencing depot_build_[DepotID].vdf scripts that map local files into depots. Files are chunked (~1MB), diffed, compressed, encrypted, and uploaded; each upload gets a BuildID you assign to a branch. (Source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/sdk/uploading)

Depot layout for Windows+macOS: create one depot per platform, set each depot's OS filter (Windows-only / macOS-only), keep shared assets in an all-OS depot if desired, and define separate launch options with 'oslist' (windows / macos) pointing at the right executable (.exe vs .app bundle). (Source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/sdk/uploading)

Use beta branches for testing: push builds to a passworded beta branch, test via the real Steam client (overlay, invites, auth all behave differently than dev builds), then promote the build to the default branch. Setting the default branch live requires phone/Steam Mobile two-factor on the uploading account. (Source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/sdk/uploading)

Submit the build for release review: Valve runs the game to check it launches, matches the store page, and follows content guidelines. Typically 1-5 business days. Multiplayer-only games should provide Valve test instructions/accounts since reviewers must be able to reach gameplay. (Sources: https://ziva.sh/blogs/publish-game-steam, https://pixune.com/blog/how-to-publish-a-game-on-steam/)

Steam Deck: Valve automatically runs a Deck compatibility review post-launch and assigns Verified/Playable/Unsupported. There is no macOS path on Deck -- it runs the WINDOWS depot under Proton on Linux, so the Windows build is what gets tested. For a chat-heavy social deduction game the make-or-break items are: text input (invoke the on-screen keyboard via ISteamUtils::ShowFloatingGamepadTextInput or you fail review), full controller support or touch fallback, legible UI/fonts at 1280x800, and any anti-cheat/networking must work under Proton. You can also request a re-review after fixes. (Sources: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/steamhardware/compat, https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/steamdeck/proton)

Realistic total timeline 2026: ~1 week onboarding + store page build, 3-5 days store review, 2+ weeks Coming Soon, 1-5 days build review, gated by the 30-day post-fee minimum -- so 4-6 weeks if everything is ready. (Source: https://ziva.sh/blogs/publish-game-steam, https://www.summerengine.com/blog/how-to-publish-game-on-steam)

steamworksFeatures.relevance: Core fit for a Mafia-style game. Steam lobbies are exactly the 'named room people join before the game starts' primitive: create lobby, set arbitrary key/value lobby metadata (room name, player count, game mode/role list), search/filter the lobby list, lobby chat before start. Important caveat from Valve's own docs: the lobby is matchmaking only -- 'the lobby itself does not facilitate multiplayer gameplay. That's your job, through your networking layer.' Free, no servers needed for the lobby phase. (Source: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/multiplayer/matchmaking)

High value, near-free virality: ISteamMatchmaking::InviteUserToLobby sends a Steam chat invite with a one-click join link; Rich Presence 'status' key shows 'In lobby 7/15 - Night 3' in the friends list and the 'connect' key enables the Join Game button on a friend's profile. Up to 20 RP keys per user, localizable. For a party game whose growth loop is 'friend sees friend playing', this is one of the highest-ROI integrations. (Sources: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/multiplayer/matchmaking, https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/api/isteamfriends)

Eliminates running your own account system entirely. Client calls ISteamUser::GetAuthTicketForWebApi('your-backend-identity-string'), sends the ticket to your backend, backend calls the ISteamUserAuth/AuthenticateUserTicket Web API with the same identity string, and gets back a verified 64-bit SteamID plus ownership/ban flags. SteamID becomes the durable player identity for stats, friends, bans, and progression -- no passwords, no email verification, no GDPR-laden credential store. Best practice: one identity string per consuming service. (Sources: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/auth, https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi/isteamuserauth)

steamworksFeatures.feature: Networking: ISteamNetworkingSockets / ISteamNetworkingMessages + Steam Datagram Relay (SDR)
steamworksFeatures.relevance: Two viable topologies for a 15-player social deduction game: (a) host-as-server P2P -- CreateListenSocketP2P/ConnectP2P automatically routes through Valve's SDR relay backbone, which hides all player IPs (critical for a game where angry players might dox/DDoS the lynch-vote winner) and often improves ping; (b) your own authoritative dedicated servers -- arguably better for Mafia since the host must not be able to read hidden roles; dedicated-server SDR access requires applying to Valve, or you can just use plain TCP/WebSockets to your own infra and use Steam only for auth/lobbies. ISteamNetworkingMessages offers a connectionless UDP-like API if preferred. (Sources: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/multiplayer/networking, https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/multiplayer/steamdatagramrelay, https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/api/ISteamnetworkingSockets)

Standard integration ('win as Jester', 'survive 10 games'); configured in the Steamworks partner site, low effort, meaningfully improves store page appeal and retention. Note for trust systems: stats are client-writable unless you push them server-side via the Web API, so don't hang anti-abuse logic off client-reported stats.

steamworksFeatures.feature: Anti-abuse: Game Bans via ICheatReportingService -- NOT VAC
steamworksFeatures.relevance: VAC is irrelevant here: it detects client-side cheat software (wallhacks, injectors) on VAC-secured servers; the abuse vector in Mafia is behavioral -- gamethrowing, chat abuse, vote-griefing, multi-accounting. What applies instead: (1) Game Bans -- developer-issued bans through the ICheatReportingService Web API (publisher key, secure-server-only); banned players get a permanent 'Game Ban' marker on their Steam profile and are blocked from secure multiplayer for the duration you set, which is the real deterrent because ban evasion costs a new game purchase; (2) your own report/review pipeline keyed on verified SteamIDs from Steam Auth (authoritative server logs chat + actions, players file reports, you or moderators issue bans); (3) ISteamUtils::FilterText -- Steam's built-in legally-required text filtering for user chat, very relevant for a chat-centric game; (4) account-quality signals (Steam account age, phone-verified, prior game bans visible via Web API) to gate ranked play. (Sources: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/anticheat, https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/webapi/ICheatReportingService, https://help.steampowered.com/en/faqs/view/46DB-4CEC-F7E9-49E5)

steam.macNotes: Valve policy since October 2019 ('Updated Requirements for New macOS Applications on Steam', https://steamcommunity.com/groups/steamworks/eventcomments/1742266164814599752/): new macOS apps on Steam must be 64-bit and must be signed + notarized with an Apple Developer ID. Practical chain: (1) join the Apple Developer Program ($99/yr) and obtain a 'Developer ID Application' certificate; (2) sign every executable, dylib, and framework in the .app bundle inside-out with codesign, using --timestamp and the hardened runtime (hardened runtime is mandatory for notarization); (3) CRITICAL Steam-specific gotcha: enable the com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation entitlement -- without Disable Library Validation the Steam overlay/Steamworks dylib injection fails and 'the app will not work right when launched from Steam' (https://blog.xojo.com/2026/03/24/code-signing-on-macos-what-developers-need-to-know-part-3/); (4) submit with notarytool (altool is dead), wait for the ticket, then staple it (stapler staple) so Gatekeeper can verify offline (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution, https://developer.apple.com/developer-id/). Nuances: files downloaded by the Steam client don't carry the quarantine xattr, so Gatekeeper often wouldn't block an unsigned app in practice -- but Valve requires notarization for new apps regardless, and signing protects users who copy the app around. Apple Silicon: ship a universal (arm64 + x86_64) binary or accept Rosetta 2 translation; for a lightweight lobby game either works, but native arm64 is increasingly expected in 2026. Architect the build pipeline so the .app is signed/notarized BEFORE the SteamPipe depot upload (SteamPipe must not modify the bundle afterward or the signature breaks -- upload the exact notarized bundle). macOS depot gets its own launch option with oslist=macos pointing at the .app. Also note Steam Deck does NOT use the macOS build -- it runs the Windows depot under Proton -- so macOS support buys you Mac players only.
steam.legalAnalysis: FRAMEWORK (not legal advice -- practical risk assessment). Three legal layers apply to cloning SC2Mafia: (1) copyright in the SC2Mafia map's expression, complicated by Blizzard's ownership claim; (2) the non-copyrightability of game mechanics; (3) trademark around names. --- LAYER 1, Blizzard's claim: Blizzard's Custom Game Acceptable Use Policy (https://www.blizzard.com/en-us/legal/2749df07-2b53-4990-b75e-a7cb3610318b/custom-game-acceptable-use-policy) states 'Custom Games are and shall remain the sole and exclusive property of Blizzard' and the creator 'hereby assign[s] to Blizzard all of your rights, title, and interest' including copyrights, and bars selling custom games. Consequence: whatever copyrightable expression exists IN the SC2Mafia map (Galaxy trigger code, in-map text, role description strings, any custom art, the map file itself) is claimed by Blizzard, and Dark.Revenant likely couldn't license it to you even if willing. So the clone must not lift anything FROM the map: no exported assets, no decompiled triggers, no verbatim text. A clean-room reimplementation of the RULES in your own engine with your own assets/text is outside the AUP's reach -- the AUP governs content made WITH Blizzard's tools, and rules/mechanics aren't ownable by anyone (see Layer 2). Enforcement reality check: the Valve-Blizzard DotA dispute (settled May 2012) shows Blizzard's actual posture -- the fight was over the 'DotA' TRADEMARK, not over copyright in mechanics; Valve kept commercial rights to the Dota name and shipped Dota 2, built openly on a WC3 custom map's design (https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/blizzard-and-valve-settle-ongoing-dota-trademark-controversy, https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Blizzard_Entertainment,_Inc._v_Valve_Corporation). Blizzard has never, as far as the record shows, sued a standalone remake of a custom map's mechanics that used original assets and a non-Blizzard name. --- LAYER 2, mechanics are not copyrightable (idea/expression distinction, 17 U.S.C. 102(b)): Tetris Holding v. Xio Interactive, 863 F.Supp.2d 394 (D.N.J. 2012) -- rules and functional gameplay are unprotectable ideas, BUT the specific audiovisual expression ('look and feel': piece colors/shapes/dimensions, board proportions, visual style) is protected; Xio lost because it copied the visuals nearly pixel-for-pixel, not because it copied falling-block rules (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetris_Holding,_LLC_v._Xio_Interactive,_Inc.). DaVinci Editrice v. ZiKo Games (S.D.
